mintedFrom.method: getNodeByIdAsync on each stem's cellNodeId (taken from parity/receipts/console-loop/visual-truth/mui/<stem>.json); cellW/cellH = node.width/node.height — the CELL BOX, the same method every other lane's mint used. fileKey 59mLQlOMiD5w5za6SUcoO5 ("MUI Test 1") was connected to the Desktop Bridge this session, which is the condition the 2026-08-08 cellPending reason named as its unblock.
mintedFrom.boxNotRenderBounds: The 2026-08-08 cellPending reason left one question open: whether the five stems whose cached box disagreed with the committed shot were genuine FC-CELL-FRAMING violations or an artifact of reading box size rather than render bounds. MEASURED THIS SESSION, and it is the latter for the disagreement and the former for the pin: exportAsync at scale 1 returned EXACTLY absoluteRenderBounds for all five (fab 44x72, linear-progress 328x4, select 75x61, snackbar 324x85, text-field 253x93), so a shot is always the RENDER box while cellW/cellH is the LAYOUT box. C1 is pinned to the LAYOUT box deliberately: pinning render bounds would make C1 compare the export to itself, and it is exactly the box-vs-ink gap that let MUI Divider ship a 288x100 transparent birth box behind a 288x1 strip of ink and score a PASSING 0.00. Where the two diverge the stem carries a cellNote with both numbers.

guard.framingCausesNote: C2 (reference comparability) is waived on a fail-closed receipt by naming ANY of these in visual.defects. A stem already retargeted to a correct like-for-like reference that still sits outside the guard names the real emit defect (FC-ABS-SIZE / FC-WIDTH-TOKEN), not the generic framing code. The mui lane adds FC-GLYPH-MOJIBAKE and FC-TEXT-WRAP: two stems (icon-button, link) have a correct, like-for-like reference and a CANVAS-side defect, and naming that defect is strictly more honest than restating 'framing'.
guard.contentCausesNote: C5 (referenceSweepCheck) ranks the canvas shot against every sibling __default gate-shot in the directory this stem’s own referenceSource names, using an 8x8x8 colour-histogram total-variation distance; it fires only on a decisive margin (pinned>=sweepPinnedMinPct AND gap>=sweepGapMinPct) and is waived on a fail-closed receipt by FC-REF-WRONG-VARIANT (retarget accepted) or FC-REF-SWEEP-DECOY (retarget examined and refused: the canvas, not the reference, is what is wrong). C6 (referenceToneCheck) applies the same distance to the pinned pair, but only in the band where the AA number is claiming closeness (pass claim, or scorecard pctAAMasked<=toneAAMaxPct) — pixelmatch at threshold 0.1 compares YIQ against a 352 cutoff, so a whole-component tone swap sits under it (measured: #F0F0F0 cell vs #D5EBFF reference, YIQ delta 158, 94.43% of pixels differing per channel, AA 7.13). Thresholds calibrated 2026-08-08 against five measured wrong-reference pairs (tv 20.6-97.3) and every committed pair in-tree (highest non-firing sweep gap 10.1pt; highest in-band tone distance 17.3%).
guard.cellOverhangNote: C1 accepts a NAMED overhang only when the committed shot equals the stem's independently-measured absoluteRenderBounds AND the entry carries an FC-* code and a reason. It cannot launder a wrong-cell or whole-set shot — those match neither the layout box plus a uniform margin nor the render box. mui/fab DOES carry one, under FC-GEOMETRY-EXCLUDED. Its 8x36 layout box is a real geometry loss, but it is a DELIBERATE, ALREADY-NAMED refusal (fuse.ts:555-565) that is independently carried by a FAILING scorecard (39.19, compositionOk false) and a fail-closed receipt — so naming it here hides nothing, and C1's own question (is this shot that cell) is honestly answered yes.
